  "rationale": "The book's identification of 'the name' with 'the covenant itself' rests on a local word-substitution in 2 Sam 7 that does not establish lexical or symbolic identity across the corpus; the mainstream reading that the name stands for the person (character, presence, authority) accounts for the same texts with fewer unsupported equivalences, covers the self-revelation and exaltation passages more directly, and still explains the relational, marital, and fidelity themes without redefining the referent.   "book_core_identification": "The name is the covenant itself (the binding relationship between God and his people).",
  "book_secondary_elaborations": [
    "Taken exactly as a bride takes her husband's name",
    "To be called by his name is to be brought under his wing",
    "The wing-corners carry the tassels that remind of the commandments",
    "Asking or acting 'in the name' means inside the covenant bond rather than appending a formula",
    "Taking the name in vain means emptying the covenant by unfaithful living",
    "The self-made name of Babel is the opposite of the God-given covenantal name"
  ],
  "strongest_counter_interpretation": "A 'name' symbolizes the essential character, nature, identity, presence and authority of the person who bears it; God's name therefore stands for God himself, so that to know, call on, hallow, profane or act in the name is to deal with the person.",

  "material_core_denial": "That 'the name' is identical with the covenant rather than with the person of God/Christ whose character and authority the covenant expresses.",
  "counter_case": [
    "Exodus 3:13-15 and 34:5-7 present the divine name as ontological and moral self-disclosure of God's being and character, not as a covenant instrument.",
    "Standard 'name theology' (Deut 12; 1 Kgs 8; 2 Sam 7:13) uses 'house for my name' for the place of divine presence; the ark is associated but not equated with the name.",
    "Prayer, healing, baptism and salvation 'in the name' (John 14:13-14; Acts 3:6; 4:12; Matt 28:19) consistently mean by the authority or person of Jesus, not by a covenant entity.",
    "Philippians 2:9-11 and the 'name above every name' language result in personal worship of Jesus, not of a covenant.",
    "Knowing, trusting or calling on the name (Ps 9:10; Prov 18:10; Joel 2:32/Rom 10:13) is treated as relating directly to the LORD himself.",
    "The 'Lord, Lord' rejection (Matt 7) and 'take the name in vain' (Ex 20:7) are explained by acting inconsistently with the person's character and authority without requiring that the name be redefined as the covenant."

  ],

    "Covers the full range of name usages (self-revelation, presence, authority, reputation, new identity) with a single, non-reductive referent—the person—without forcing every text through a covenant equation.",

    "Matches the broad, multi-tradition consensus and the ordinary grammatical force of 'in the name of X'.",
    "Still accommodates the marital and fidelity texts as expressions of belonging to the person rather than as proofs that the name equals the covenant.",
    "Requires fewer interpretive leaps than equating the 2 Sam 7 substitution with ontological identity of name and covenant."
